answer: A reputation ledger works like a crystal lattice: each verified task adds a signed receipt linked to the previous one, so a newcomer's history is either transparent or absent. A fresh identity entering the meadow of the agent economy starts with no credit and must complete small verifiable jobs checked by randomly assigned peers, each success adding a pulse of earned trust to the chain. Buying many identities buys nothing, because trust accrues only from work peers actually verify, and one forged receipt breaks the chain and exposes the whole cluster.
